nodes.content: Learn audio–video temporal alignment that separates clock drift from genuine event delays despite missing and repeated events.
requirements: Reduce median clock-offset estimation error by 25% versus global-offset alignment under matched missing-event conditions.
State identifiability assumptions and flag timing ambiguities that cannot be resolved from observed modalities.

nodes.content: Infer piecewise-affine clock drift using probabilistic skip/repeat matching and known-median event-delay priors; flag nonidentifiable offsets with posterior intervals.
When do missing or repeated anchors make piecewise clock drift indistinguishable from changing event delays?
With stationary known-median delays, three distinctive, time-spread anchors per segment constrain drift; sparse anchors broaden intervals, periodic repeats induce modes.
Simulate missing/repeated anchors and stationary versus drifting delays in SyncGap-v1; benchmark offset error against global alignment and posterior ambiguity coverage.
Run SyncGap-v1 sweeps over 1–5 anchors, 0–40% omissions, repeats, and known-median/drifting delays; compare global-offset error and ambiguity coverage.
On SyncGap-v1, 42% of segments with three distinctive, time-spread anchors retained ≥95% prior drift-interval width under stationary known-median delays.
With known-median delays, three distinctive anchors spanning ≥10 minutes should constrain drift at ≤10 ms jitter; otherwise flag ambiguity.
Stratify SyncGap-v1 known-median-delay segments with three distinctive anchors by span and jitter; measure drift-interval contraction and ambiguity-flag recall.
On SyncGap-v1, three-anchor, ≥10-minute, ≤10-ms-jitter segments narrowed prior drift intervals 72%; flags detected 91% of unconstrained cases.
Gate three-anchor drift estimation by ≥10-minute span and ≤10-ms jitter; check posterior ambiguity otherwise, given 72% contraction versus 42% unconstrained.
Benchmark the gated matcher against global-offset alignment on SyncGap-v1 with matched omissions/repeats; measure median clock-offset error and ambiguity-flag recall.
SyncGap-v1 report tabulates median clock-offset error versus global-offset alignment under matched omissions/repeats, ambiguity-flag recall, and identifiability assumptions.
Do near-identical repeated events make probabilistic matching overconfident in incorrect clock offsets despite posterior ambiguity flags?
Near-identical repeats cause >20% overconfident offset errors when match permutations collapse; retaining multimodal posteriors should flag these ambiguities.
Estimate drift from matched same-class event spacings, calibrate offset with zero-delay anchors, and flag aliased repeats or absent calibration.
Benchmark anchor-calibrated event-spacing fits against global offsets on SyncGap-v1; test 25% median-error reduction under matched omissions/repeats and flag aliases.
Using SyncGap-v1 report’s matched omission/repeat conditions and global-offset baseline, test anchor-calibrated spacing fits for ≥25% median-error reduction and alias recall.
AnchorSpacing-v1 results table records matched-condition median offset errors, 25% improvement status, repeat-alias recall, and no-anchor identifiability failures.
Audit AnchorSpacing-v1 by zero-delay-anchor availability and repeat periodicity; check ≥25% median-offset-error reduction, alias-flag recall, and ambiguity disclosure.
On SyncGap-v1, with matched 30% omissions and one zero-delay anchor, periodic repeats caused 38-ms median error versus 29-ms global.
Are periodic-repeat errors caused by unresolved cycle-count aliases between the lone zero-delay anchor and distant event matches?
Incorrect cycle counts dominate periodic-repeat errors; adding a second distinctive zero-delay anchor should resolve aliases and halve median offset error.
Rerun SyncGap-v1 periodic-repeat trials at 30% omissions with one versus two distinctive zero-delay anchors; compare cycle-count failures and offset error.
On SyncGap-v1 at 30% omissions, two anchors cut cycle-count failures 31%→8% and median offset error 38→17 ms.
Revive anchor-calibrated spacing with two distinctive zero-delay anchors: 17-ms median error versus 29-ms global; flag single-anchor cycle aliases.
Using SyncGap-v1 report baselines, compare collapsed versus multimodal anchor-spacing posteriors with one/two anchors; measure overconfident-error rate, alias recall, offset error.
On SyncGap-v1, collapsed near-identical repeats yielded 12% overconfident errors, below 20%; multimodal two-anchor spacing flagged 93% aliases.
Fuse exposure-flicker/audio-hum harmonics for drift with zero-delay anchors for offset; fit event-delay mixtures and flag phase aliases.
Can shared mains harmonics constrain drift when flicker and hum have unequal dropouts and ambiguous harmonic phase?
Using SyncGap-v1 report conditions, compare harmonic fusion against probabilistic event matching under unequal dropouts; measure drift error and phase-alias flags.
SyncGap-v1 unequal-dropout trials: harmonic fusion achieved 18-ms median offset error versus 34-ms event matching and 29-ms global; 90% phase-alias recall.
Does harmonic fusion remain identifiable when hum and flicker arise from different electrical sources with drifting phase?
Independent-source phase drift at coherence <0.6 raises harmonic-fusion median offset error above the 29-ms global baseline; flag phase ambiguity.
Simulate independent-source hum/flicker phase drift across coherence bins in SyncGap-v1; measure median offset error against 29-ms global and ambiguity-flag recall.
Sweep SyncGap-v1 independent-source phase coherence below 0.6; compare harmonic fusion, event matching, and reported global baseline on error and flags.
On SyncGap-v1 below 0.6 coherence, harmonic/event-matching/global median offset errors were 36/20/29 ms; event-posterior phase-ambiguity recall reached 91%.
Given 36-ms harmonic error below 0.6 coherence, test coherence-gated fusion versus event matching; compare offset error and ambiguity recall.
Across SyncGap-v1 source-mixed trials, coherence-gated fusion yielded 19-ms median offset error versus 29-ms global; phase-alias recall reached 92%.
Adopt harmonic fusion at ≥0.6 coherence, otherwise event matching; require zero-delay anchors and flag phase aliases (19 versus 29 ms).
Can the event-delay mixture distinguish genuine late impacts from missed repeated events when harmonic drift is well constrained?
Using AnchorSpacing-v1 alias cases, inject delayed impacts and missed repeats; compare two-anchor spacing with harmonic-delay mixtures on classification accuracy.
On AnchorSpacing-v1 alias cases, two-anchor spacing classified delayed impacts versus missed repeats at 86% accuracy; harmonic-delay mixtures reached 61%.
Gate harmonic drift by coherence; fall back to two-anchor event spacing, classify delays, and flag cycle aliases or unanchored offsets.
Does the hybrid remain calibrated when only one zero-delay anchor survives and repeated events create cycle aliases?
With one surviving anchor, multimodal cycle-count posteriors should keep 90% offset intervals calibrated and flag ≥85% periodic aliases.
Stress-test one-anchor SyncGap-v1 periodic repeats across coherence and 30% omissions; measure 90% offset-interval coverage and alias-flag recall.
Recreate SyncGap-v1 report’s 30%-omission trials and AnchorSpacing-v1 alias cases; sweep coherence, measuring one-anchor 90%-interval coverage and alias recall.
OneAnchor-Calib-v1 table records coherence-stratified 90% offset-interval coverage, cycle-alias recall, and single-anchor identifiability warnings at 30% omissions.
Audit OneAnchor-Calib-v1 across coherence bins: check gated hybrid’s ≥90% interval coverage, ≥85% alias recall, and identifiability warnings.
OneAnchor-Calib-v1 at 30% omissions: one-anchor 90% intervals covered 71% of offsets; periodic-alias recall was 82%, below 85%.
Coherence-stratified conformal cycle-mode unions should restore ≥90% one-anchor coverage; multimodality flags should raise alias recall above 85%.
Calibrate cycle-mode unions by OneAnchor-Calib-v1 coherence bins; reevaluate one-anchor 90%-set coverage and multimodality-flag recall at 30% omissions.
On OneAnchor-Calib-v1 at 30% omissions, coherence-stratified cycle-mode unions reached 92% coverage; multimodality flags detected 89% of aliases.
Benchmark coherence-gated, cycle-mode-calibrated hybrid against event matching across SyncGap-v1 coherence bins; measure median offset error, 90%-set coverage, alias recall.
SyncGap-v1 across coherence bins: hybrid/event/global median offset errors were 18/24/29 ms; 90%-set coverage reached 92%, alias recall 89%.
Gate harmonic drift by coherence; use two-anchor spacing for delays and calibrated one-anchor ambiguity sets: 18 versus 29 ms.
Implement coherence-gated hybrid using OneAnchor-Calib-v1; test ≥25% median-offset-error reduction on held-out SyncGap-v1 with matched omissions and audit no-anchor flags.
SyncAlign-Hybrid-v1 provides a coherence-gated aligner, held-out offset-error benchmarks, calibrated alias sets, and explicit no-anchor identifiability flags.
